JNJ.rationale: JNJ is a high-quality franchise with genuine growth catalysts (Q1 2026 revenue +9.9% YoY, Innovative Medicine +11.2%, PROTEUS and JASMINE pipeline readouts), but the stock has re-rated so aggressively (+50.9% over 52 weeks) that the quantitative picture is now deeply unfavorable. PE of 26.5x is near the 365-day ceiling (range 16.6–27.2x), representing ~55% multiple expansion in 12 months from 17.1x. Earnings yield of 3.8% now sits below the 10-year Treasury yield of 4.47%, eliminating the defensive yield premium that historically justified holding JNJ. Margins are compressing: Q4 operating margin fell to 24.9% from Q3's 31.2%, gross margin declined to 66.3% from 69.6%, and cost of revenue rose 11% QoQ on flat revenue. Q4 operating cash flow collapsed 72.6% QoQ to $2.51B. Net margin has slipped to 0.218 from a stable 0.273. The market is paying a near-record multiple for deteriorating profitability. A mean-reversion of PE to the 18–20x midrange on normalized EPS of ~$8.7 annualized implies $157–$174, or 24–31% downside. Rising rates (10Y at 4.47%, up 8.5% over 90 days) further compress the justified PE for a low-growth defensive. Talc litigation remains an unresolved overhang. The qualitative franchise quality is real but fully priced and then some — the stock has run far ahead of fundamentals.
